intro.text: Syl, a playful spren who has attached herself to Kaladin, a bridgeman, and talks with him though others cannot see her.
Syl, a spren who has remembered her true nature and formed a bond with Kaladin that lets him draw on Stormlight and Surgebind.
Syl is an honorspren bonded to Kaladin as a Windrunner. Since he swore the Third Ideal, she can become a Shardblade, spear or other weapon for him.
Syl is the honorspren bonded to Kaladin. When he spoke the Words to join the Oathpact after the Stormfather's death, it was her voice that accepted them.

items.text: Syl had been found and reawakened after more than a thousand years. The Stormfather set Notum to keep her safe in an honorspren city, but she ran away to bond Kaladin, and her kin offered a bounty for her return to Lasting Integrity.
Syl had followed Kaladin, nearly mindless, since his days in Amaram's army, regaining her wits as she stayed near him.

Syl first spoke to Kaladin after he found and kept some leaves of the poison blackbane; he thought he was going mad, but in time answered her. She stayed with him, urging him to get up during his first bridge run, but as he sank deeper into despair she said she could not bear to watch and left.

Remembering that blackbane had once given Kaladin hope, and not knowing what it was for, Syl went to find more. She returned to find him on the edge of the Honor Chasm about to end his life. After a great struggle she brought him a leaf, which amused him, and she persuaded him to give life another try.

Syl supported Kaladin as he tried to win over Bridge Four, spying on Gaz for him and then watching over the other bridgemen too. She kept asking him about people, hoping to understand humans, and when she first saw Dalinar Kholin she decided he was honorable, despite Kaladin's doubts.
Syl and Kaladin discovered that Rock, one of the bridgemen, could see her. On chasm duty she helped the two of them search for valuables, and she kept spying on Gaz.

When Kaladin was strung up in a highstorm as punishment, Syl stayed with him, trying to hold back the storm and then fighting off the deathspren drawn to him with a sword. Afterward she began to recall fragments of her past, delighting in the First Ideal of the Knights Radiant and hissing at the mention of Odium.

When Kaladin's Surgebinding began to show, Syl admitted she was no ordinary windspren and that their bond was changing them both. At his urging she showed herself to all of Bridge Four, and she pushed him to train his abilities.

At the Battle of the Tower, Syl appeared as a full-sized figure and remembered what she truly was. She persuaded Kaladin to go back for the Kholin troops and to say the Immortal Words. Afterward she urged him to trust Dalinar, and Bridge Four became the Kholin guard.

Syl's respect for Dalinar grew after he gave up a Shardblade to free the bridgemen. She told Kaladin there might be other Surgebinders, noticed stormspren about, and insisted he become what Dalinar needed. When Amaram arrived, she pressed Kaladin to tell Dalinar honestly what Amaram had done to him.

As Kaladin began backsliding on his oaths, Syl grew worried but stayed by him. She warned him when Szeth came to attack, saw at once that Szeth was not a true Surgebinder, and was surprised to learn Kaladin could heal Shardblade wounds.

Syl kept insisting Dalinar could be trusted, even after Kaladin learned of Moash's plot against Elhokar. She taught Kaladin more about Surgebinding as he learned to fly, and convinced him things would be different at Adolin's four-on-one duel. She was wrong; when Kaladin demanded to duel Amaram, he was arrested.

As Kaladin strayed from his oaths, Syl began losing her higher mind until she effectively died. When he finally stood to protect Elhokar, she tried to return, but the Stormfather, who had been sheltering her to keep her from truly dying, held her back. Their weakened bond let her speak in Kaladin's mind, and when he swore the Third Ideal she returned as a ribbon of light and then a Shardblade.

Syl and Kaladin drove off Moash and Graves, then flew to protect Dalinar from Szeth in the chaos of the battle at Narak. She shifted into many different weapons during the fight, and Kaladin used her to cut through Szeth's wrist and take his Honorblade. Afterward she demanded a smile from Kaladin, and got one.

Traveling with Kaladin, Syl began worrying about his happiness and decided he needed a romantic partner. She teased him about girls they met, admitted she had spied on people in intimate moments, and quietly hoped to pair him with Shallan, who seemed to make him happy.

When Kaladin let a group of former parshmen take him, Syl noticed a voidspren with them and pretended to be a windspren to fool her. In private, she admitted she did not know why killing singers did not feel wrong to her when killing humans did.

After seeing a Fused in Rathalas, Syl and Kaladin left in a highstorm and returned to Urithiru, where he trained his squires. Syl spotted some honorspren she had known, who disliked her even though they too were now seeking bondmates.

Syl went with Kaladin to Thaylen City and then to besieged Kholinar with Elhokar, Adolin and Shallan. She was the first to notice the city's corrupted spren, helped Kaladin as he worked with the Wall Guard, and pointed him to a Fused's gemheart, the quickest way to kill it.

Syl fought as Kaladin's weapon in the battle for Kholinar Palace and was shaken when he killed a voidspren. When the group tried to work the Oathgate, she, Kaladin, Adolin, Shallan, Pattern and Azure were dropped into Shadesmar.

In Shadesmar, Syl took a human-sized form and behaved more like a physical being. She focused on keeping Kaladin going through his breakdown, and explained that she would lose her mind if she went too far from him, so she could not carry a message to Dalinar.

On the journey, Syl told Kaladin some of her past and mentioned that other spren disliked honorspren. In Celebrant she admitted her kin had placed a bounty on her. Fleeing the Fused, she called to the honorspren ship Honor's Path, captained by her old minder Notum, getting the group aboard at the cost of being taken prisoner. As Kaladin neared the Fourth Ideal and spoke of a Stormfather Bondsmith, Notum let them go.

During the fight for Thaylen City's Oathgate, Syl joined Shallan's illusory distraction. When things went badly, she pulled Kaladin from the sea of beads and urged him to say the Fourth Ideal. When he could not, she held and comforted him, just as Honor's Perpendicularity opened.

Back in the Physical Realm, Syl fought as Kaladin's weapon in the Battle of Thaylen Field. Afterward they discussed whether fighting the singers was right; Kaladin chose to keep fighting for humanity and promised never to kill her or any other sapient spren. They then went to rescue Skar and Drehy, who had brought Gavinor out of Kholinar.

About a year after Thaylen Field, Syl and Kaladin slipped into Hearthstone among refugees and barely escaped a fight with the Fused Lezian. Syl badgered Kaladin about how tired he looked, entertained his brother Oroden, told his mother Hesina that he and Lyn had split up, and went with him to see his father.

Syl and Kaladin fought the Fused Leshwi in the air. Kaladin realized Syl had asked Bridge Four to keep an eye on him; she explained she had kept his nightmares secret because telling would only make them worse. Their duel with Leshwi was even until Leshwi let them go to save civilians at the manor.

At the manor, a Voidlight fabrial forced Syl out of Blade form and stripped Kaladin's powers, though he still killed Lezian. In the cellar, as a spear in Kaladin's hands, she could not reach him while Moash urged him toward suicide, until Renarin's illusion drove Moash away. Afterward she admitted she did not know how to help him.

Syl relayed the windspren Yunfah's complaints to Kaladin and urged him to keep pushing Yunfah to bond Rlain. At Narak she apologized to Dalinar for her honorspren kin and watched anxiously as Dalinar relieved Kaladin of duty. Back in Urithiru she fetched Adolin to drag Kaladin out for an evening.

Syl became a dulled sword so Kaladin could spar with Zahel, though they lost. When his parents arrived, she eagerly showed them the rooms she and Kaladin had prepared and prompted Kaladin to tell Lirin he had retired and wanted to help in his clinic.

During a highstorm, Syl asked the Stormfather to help her understand Kaladin's depression; he said he had the power but not the ability. She went to Dalinar, who helped her see that the feelings that made her drift after Relador's death might help her understand Kaladin's dark moods.

Syl warned Adolin not to expect too much from his embassy to the honorspren and gave him tips on their sense of morality. In the clinic, she read medical notes for Kaladin and talked with him about using their powers for things other than war, and was saddened that the Windrunners were leaving for Azir.

When the enemy began corrupting Urithiru's crystal pillar, Syl was suddenly cut off from Kaladin and only found her way back to him with his help. She could no longer become a Blade or travel far from him without losing herself, but brought word that Navani knew of the invasion as more enemies poured through the Oathgates.

Syl acted like a windspren to fool the invaders while scouting for Kaladin. After Navani's surrender, she spotted soldiers searching for Teft, and she and Kaladin rescued him. She tried to lure the Pursuer away, then spotted a mysterious light that guided them to a hidden room, and she guessed that the Sibling was behind it.

Syl helped Kaladin gather supplies and check on his parents. She finally told him her melancholy came from remembering Relador. Learning that spren were more visible in the corrupted tower, she disguised herself in red cloth as a voidspren to distract guards while Kaladin stole spanreeds, until the Sibling asked for help defending a node.

Syl's voidspren act distracted the Pursuer long enough for Kaladin to trap him and destroy the node. She studied the captured spanreeds and found their spren were corrupted much like Glys, letting them run on Voidlight. She also tried to wake Kaladin from his nightmares.

Syl woke Kaladin with news of another node in the Breakaway and guided him through the fight and down into a well to destroy it. When the Pursuer sealed the well with Kaladin below, she panicked and slipped into a state like the one she had fallen into after Relador's death, until Kaladin called to her and she broke back through.

Syl and Kaladin raced to stop the execution of the Radiants and were crushed to find Teft dead. Following a Fused who had taken Lirin, Syl wept that she had forgotten the Fourth Ideal as Kaladin leapt from the tower. He returned from a vision and reached for her, and together they saved Lirin and rejoined the fight.

After Teft's funeral, Syl encouraged Kaladin to ask Dalinar to let him continue helping people with mental illness. Told they had only ten days before the contest of champions, they agreed to go to Shinovar to help heal the mad Herald Ishar.

On the first of the final ten days, Syl explained that she now appeared at human size because people treated her more like a person that way. She and Kaladin talked about his improved state, their grief for Teft and the battles ahead. She sensed something on the wind, though she could not hear the voice that spoke to Kaladin.

Syl found Wit teaching Kaladin the flute. On a mountain peak, she stayed visible to Dalinar and joined the conversation, which he found unusual for an honorspren. When Dalinar asked Kaladin to be his heir, she assured him royalty was not so bad.

Syl and Kaladin said goodbye to Bridge Four; Syl collected a copy of The Way of Kings and writing supplies, and Kaladin scolded librarians who scoffed at her writing. Leaving with Szeth, they bid farewell to Adolin and Shallan in Azimir, and Syl worried Kaladin seemed to expect not to return.

In Shinovar, Syl comforted Kaladin when Szeth would not open up. The Wind spoke to them of Odium, and Ishar came but would not help, puzzling them by calling Szeth his servant. At Szeth's family farmhouse, Syl explained that spren sensed something was wrong in Shinovar, and admitted she needed to start living for herself, not only for Kaladin.

Syl translated for Kaladin at the Bondsmith monastery and urged Szeth to accept Kaladin's help. In camp she read to Kaladin from The Way of Kings and scribed reports to Urithiru, and the two danced a kata together, Syl shifting between spear and human form while the Wind joined in.

Finding Szeth crying over a toy sheep, Syl helped Kaladin see that Szeth himself was the child he mourned. At the Lightweaver monastery, she secretly guided Szeth through a test among illusions, then warned Kaladin of a second attacker, and he summoned her as a spear in time to save Szeth.

Syl sensed a change in her bond with Kaladin and came to empathize somewhat with Szeth's highspren despite her distrust. The Wind showed them visions of Nale saving people and asked them to help the Heralds. When Nale admitted Szeth's pilgrimage was a trial to replace Jezrien, Syl argued against his reasoning.

When Nale tried to kill Szeth for refusing his vow, Kaladin blocked with Syl as a spear. During the long duel she reminded Kaladin of Nale's past hunts for Radiants, and stood in Nale's way when he moved for the kill. When the Wind began playing, Kaladin summoned her as a flute and told Nale the story of Derethil until the Herald broke down weeping.

When Nale explained there was no Unmade in Shinovar, Syl worked out that the Voice Szeth had heard was Ishar. At the final monastery Ishar dismissed their song and forced the Heralds' anguish on everyone; Syl collapsed until Kaladin swore his Fifth Ideal and freed them.

With Dalinar and the Stormfather dead, all spren were in danger of being consumed. Syl wept, knowing what Kaladin must do. When he spoke the Words to join the Oathpact, her voice accepted them; together they drew a Shardspear from the circle of Honorblades, and she held his hand as his soul left Roshar.

appearance.text: As a weapon, Syl appears as glowing silvery metal engraved with glyphs, most often a spear with a helical swirl near the tip, but also a sword or shield. As a sword she is sleek, with a Windrunner glyph whose lines recall her hair.

Syl usually appears as a tiny young woman in a flowing, girlish dress, barefoot, with hair that fades into mist, all glowing blue-white; she can also become a ribbon of light, leaves or a cloud, and is invisible to most unless she chooses. In Shadesmar she is human-sized and cannot change form.

personality.text: Syl is cheerful and mischievous, fond of jokes and pranks, irreverent and sometimes forgetful. She is relentlessly optimistic and sees the best in people. She has a playful proud streak, calling herself a tiny piece of god, and an endless curiosity about people that leads her to spy on them invisibly with little sense of propriety.

She holds a strict moral code and despises lies, though she grows more willing to be cunning. She believes a Windrunner's power is justified only to protect others, and can be forceful and angry when someone acts wrongly. She hates the wielding of dead Shardblades, and grows uneasy when the war's sides blur.

Syl wants to be seen as a person, not just a spren. She appears at human size, lets more people see her, and looks for things to do for her own sake, such as writing and keeping a journal, while struggling to balance this with helping Kaladin.
